title: Only 7% Pass This Nursing Entrance Exam
summary: Anatomy, vital signs, safety, numeracy and patient-care judgement get harder across 10 stages.

landing.intro: Think you have the knowledge, calm judgement and people skills to make it through the challenge?

about.body:
This Clinical Admissions Lab turns entrance-level nursing knowledge into ten increasingly demanding stages. The questions cover anatomy and physiology, healthcare numeracy, observation trends, infection prevention, patient communication and calm clinical prioritisation.

The challenge is designed for curious adults, prospective nursing students and healthcare learners around the world. It uses universal principles such as noticing deterioration, protecting dignity, reducing infection risk, communicating clearly and seeking appropriate qualified help—never country-specific policies or specialist treatment decisions.

Your final score reflects only the answers given in this entertainment quiz. It is a playful snapshot of the entrance areas that felt strongest and the topics that proved more challenging, not a judgement of clinical competence or suitability for nursing.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Answer six questions in each stage and choose the single response best supported by the visible information.
Correct answers stay hidden while you play, so read every chart, clue and patient statement carefully.
Complete all ten stages to reveal your Nursing Score, strongest entrance area and full answer review.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited nursing entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Healthcare procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local policy and qualified clinical guidance.

profiles.title: The Nursing Natural

profiles.title: The Calm Candidate
profiles.copy: You handled a broad mix of body knowledge, safety decisions and patient scenarios with steady reasoning. A few finer details kept the entrance challenge interesting.

profiles.title: The Careful Problem-Solver
profiles.copy: You built a solid result by following the evidence and treating patient safety seriously. Your strongest stage shows where your clinical-learning instincts are already taking shape.

profiles.title: The Promising Applicant
profiles.copy: You solved a good share of the admissions lab and showed useful instincts across several care areas. The answer review will reveal which concepts are ready for another look.

profiles.title: The Compassionate Explorer
profiles.copy: The lab uncovered some knowledge gaps, but it also found moments of thoughtful, patient-centred judgement. Every explanation is a fresh chance to strengthen the foundations behind safe care.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
questions.explanation: The heart contracts to move blood through the circulation.

questions.question: A jug contains 750 mL. Another 250 mL is added. What is the total?
questions.explanation: 750 mL plus 250 mL equals 1,000 mL, which is 1 litre.

questions.question: A pulse changes from 72 to 88 beats per minute. What does the chart show?

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse was 72 and is now 88 beats per minute

questions.explanation: The recorded pulse has increased from 72 to 88 beats per minute.

questions.question: Your hands are visibly dirty. What is the appropriate cleaning method?
answers: Wipe them on a dry towel
questions.explanation: Soap and water are appropriate when hands are visibly soiled.

questions.question: A person says, “I’m worried about what happens next.” What is the best first response?
answers: Acknowledge the worry and ask what concerns them most
Say there is nothing to worry about
Change the subject to distract them
Use technical terms to sound reassuring
questions.explanation: Acknowledging the emotion and listening first helps clarify the person’s concern without dismissing it.

questions.question: Who needs attention first?
questions.context: Person A is comfortable and asks for water. Person B has suddenly become pale and is struggling to breathe.
answers: Person A, because they asked first
Person B, because the sudden breathing problem may be an immediate danger
Both can wait until the next routine check
questions.explanation: Sudden breathing difficulty and pallor signal possible immediate deterioration and require urgent qualified help.

questions.question: Which route correctly follows oxygen into the circulation?
questions.explanation: Oxygen travels through the airway to the lungs, then crosses into the blood.

questions.question: What is a main function of the kidneys?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter the blood, regulate fluid balance and form urine containing wastes.

questions.question: Which body system carries rapid electrical signals?
questions.explanation: The nervous system uses electrical and chemical signals to communicate rapidly around the body.

questions.question: Where are most digested nutrients absorbed into the body?
questions.explanation: Most nutrient absorption takes place across the lining of the small intestine.

questions.question: Which change in this observation note matters most?
questions.context: Earlier: breathing comfortably and speaking normally. Now: breathing faster and pausing between short phrases.
answers: The note contains two time points
questions.explanation: Faster breathing with shorter speech is a meaningful change from the person’s earlier condition.

questions.question: Which person needs attention first?
questions.context: Person A is comfortable with a routine question. Person B has new chest discomfort, looks clammy and says they feel faint.
answers: Person A, because routine questions are quick
Both should wait for the next planned round
Person B, because several new signs suggest sudden deterioration
questions.explanation: New chest discomfort, clamminess and faintness together require urgent qualified assessment.

questions.question: How many millilitres are in 1.5 litres?
questions.explanation: One litre is 1,000 mL, so 1.5 litres is 1,500 mL.

questions.question: How much time passes from 09:20 to 10:05?
questions.explanation: There are 40 minutes to 10:00, then 5 more minutes to 10:05: 45 minutes total.

questions.question: A person drinks 300 mL, 250 mL and 200 mL. What is the total?
What is 25% of 200?
questions.explanation: 25% is one quarter, and one quarter of 200 is 50.

questions.question: You count 9 breaths in 30 seconds. What is the rate per minute?
questions.explanation: Thirty seconds is half a minute, so doubling 9 gives 18 breaths per minute.

questions.question: A fluid chart uses mL, but one entry says 0.4 L. What should happen before calculating the total?
answers: Add the numbers without considering units
questions.explanation: Values must use the same unit before they are combined; 0.4 L is 400 mL.

questions.question: What should happen after protective gloves are removed?
answers: Only clean hands if the gloves tore
questions.explanation: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene; hands should be cleaned after glove removal.

questions.question: Where should a used sharp item be placed?
answers: Directly into an approved puncture-resistant sharps container
questions.explanation: Used sharps belong directly in an appropriate puncture-resistant sharps container to reduce injury risk.

questions.question: A task may splash body fluid towards the face. Which protection addresses that stated risk?
answers: No protection if the task is brief
questions.explanation: Eye or face protection is selected when the risk assessment identifies possible splashes to the face.

questions.question: Shared observation equipment has just been used. What is the safest next step?
answers: Put it straight back without checking
Clean it appropriately before the next person
Cover it with paper and reuse it
Only clean it at the end of the week
questions.explanation: Reusable shared equipment should be cleaned appropriately between people to reduce transmission risk.

questions.question: A coughing person seems embarrassed. What is the best response?
answers: Tell them off in front of everyone
Offer practical respiratory-hygiene support respectfully and protect their dignity
Discuss their symptoms loudly across the room
questions.explanation: A respectful offer of practical hygiene support addresses infection risk without shaming the person.

questions.question: Which task comes first?
questions.context: A body-fluid spill is creating a slip and exposure hazard in a walkway. A storage shelf also needs routine restocking.
answers: Restock the shelf because it was planned
Leave both jobs for the next shift
Walk around the spill without warning anyone
Secure the immediate hazard and arrange appropriate cleaning
questions.explanation: The immediate environmental and exposure hazard comes before routine restocking.

questions.question: Which observation was recorded as 74?
questions.explanation: The study card recorded the pulse as 74.

questions.question: Which measurement changed while the others stayed the same?

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse unchanged, breathing increased, temperature unchanged, alertness unchanged

questions.explanation: Breathing changed from 16 to 24 while the other recorded observations stayed the same.

questions.question: Which detail describes a new change?
questions.context: Earlier: walking steadily and feeling well. Now: dizzy on standing and noticeably pale.
answers: The person stood up at some point
questions.explanation: Dizziness on standing with new pallor is the meaningful change from the earlier condition.

questions.question: What mismatch should be clarified?

visual.ariaLabel: Handover says left arm, chart says right arm

questions.explanation: The handover and chart identify different sides, so the discrepancy needs clarification.

questions.question: Which system allows pupils to respond rapidly to light?
questions.explanation: The nervous system detects light and controls the rapid pupil response.

questions.question: What is the safest interpretation?
questions.context: A person was alert and comfortable earlier. They are now unusually drowsy, clammy and breathing faster.
answers: The changes can be ignored because no diagnosis is known
Several new changes suggest deterioration and need prompt qualified assessment
Wait until tomorrow to compare again
questions.explanation: A cluster of new changes from the person’s baseline indicates possible deterioration and should be escalated promptly.

questions.question: A person says, “I’m scared about the test.” What is the best response?
answers: Everyone has tests, so try not to think about it
I promise the result will be fine
I can see this is worrying you. What concerns you most?
Use a long technical explanation immediately
questions.explanation: The response acknowledges the emotion and invites the person to explain their specific concern.

questions.question: A person says they did not understand an explanation. What is best?
answers: Repeat the same jargon more loudly
Tell them to search online later
Rephrase it plainly, then ask them to explain it back in their own words
questions.explanation: Plain language plus a respectful check of understanding makes communication clearer without blame.

questions.question: Someone asks a sensitive question in a busy public area. What should you do?
answers: Offer to continue the conversation somewhere private
Answer loudly so everyone can hear
Discuss the details with nearby visitors
questions.explanation: Moving the conversation to a private setting protects confidentiality and dignity.

questions.question: A person hesitates and says, “I’m not sure I want to continue.” What is the best response?
answers: Listen, clarify their concern and seek appropriate qualified help if needed
Make an unsupported promise that nothing can go wrong
questions.explanation: Listening and clarifying respects the person while allowing appropriate support or escalation.

questions.question: A shared communication device has been handled during care. What should happen before another person uses it?
answers: Clean it appropriately according to the stated infection-control process
Only clean the screen if it looks dusty
questions.explanation: Frequently touched shared equipment should be cleaned appropriately between users.

questions.question: A relative answers every question for an alert adult who is trying to speak. What is the best first step?
answers: Continue speaking only to the relative
Ask the relative to make every decision
Discuss the person’s details in the corridor
Address the person directly and check how they want the conversation handled
questions.explanation: Addressing the person directly protects autonomy, dignity and their communication preferences.

questions.question: Who needs attention first?
questions.context: Person A is comfortable with a mildly faster pulse after walking. Person B is suddenly confused, breathing rapidly and looks pale.
answers: Person B, because several new signs suggest sudden deterioration
Person A, because their pulse changed
Both can wait for routine observations
questions.explanation: New confusion, rapid breathing and pallor together make Person B the immediate priority.

questions.question: Which situation comes first?
questions.context: Person A asks for a blanket and is speaking comfortably. Person B has new breathing difficulty and cannot finish a sentence.
questions.explanation: New breathing difficulty that limits speech signals an immediate airway or breathing concern.

questions.question: Who needs prompt help?
questions.context: Person A is waiting for routine paperwork. Person B has fresh bleeding through a dressing and feels increasingly dizzy.
answers: Person A, because paperwork prevents delay
Both can wait until the next round
Person B, because bleeding plus dizziness may signal circulation risk
Neither person because no diagnosis is confirmed
questions.explanation: Active bleeding with increasing dizziness may threaten circulation and needs prompt qualified attention.

questions.question: Which person is the immediate priority?
questions.context: Person A has mild tingling after leaning on an arm and it is improving. Person B is choking, cannot speak and appears distressed.
answers: Person A, because tingling involves nerves
Person B, because the airway may be blocked
questions.explanation: A person who is choking and unable to speak may have a blocked airway, which is an immediate danger.

questions.question: Which change needs prompt attention?
questions.context: Person A’s observations are unchanged and they are chatting normally. Person B was alert earlier but is now drowsy, clammy and difficult to engage.
answers: Person B’s new change from alert to drowsy and clammy
The fact that both people were observed
Neither, because exact numbers are not shown
questions.explanation: The important clue is Person B’s major new change from their earlier condition.

questions.question: What is the best first response?
questions.context: Person A asks for a general leaflet. Person B quietly says they feel unsafe discussing a private concern where others can hear.
answers: Give Person B a public answer immediately
Acknowledge Person B and arrange a private conversation
Tell Person B to speak louder
Discuss the concern with the group
questions.explanation: Acknowledging the concern and moving to privacy protects dignity and enables safer communication.

questions.question: Which organs exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: Gas exchange takes place in the lungs.

questions.question: 500 mL plus 0.5 L equals?
questions.explanation: 0.5 L is 500 mL, so the total is 1,000 mL or 1 L.

questions.question: Half of 600 mL?
questions.explanation: Half of 600 mL is 300 mL.

questions.question: Which chart shows a rising pulse?
questions.explanation: 70 to 82 is the only sequence that rises.

questions.question: Gloves removed. What comes next?
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene follows glove removal.

questions.question: Best response to “I’m frightened”?
questions.explanation: Acknowledging the fear and listening addresses the person’s emotion without making unsupported promises.

questions.question: Which body-function detail changed?
questions.context: HANDOVER NOTE — Earlier: right and left hand grip equal. Now: right grip unchanged, left grip weaker than before. Feet move equally.
questions.explanation: The note directly states that the left hand grip is weaker than before.

questions.question: What total belongs in the handover?
questions.context: FLUID NOTE — Morning drink: 0.4 L. Midday drink: 350 mL. Record the combined amount in mL.
questions.explanation: 0.4 L equals 400 mL; adding 350 mL gives 750 mL.

questions.question: Which recorded measurement changed?
questions.context: SHIFT CHART — Pulse 76 → 88. Breathing 16 → 16. Temperature 37.0 → 37.0. Fluid total unchanged.
questions.explanation: Only the pulse changed, rising from 76 to 88.

questions.question: Which safety detail is missing?
questions.context: HANDOVER NOTE — Gloves removed after care. Clean equipment prepared for the next person. No hand-cleaning step recorded.
questions.explanation: The note omits hand hygiene after the gloves were removed.

questions.question: Which detail is most relevant to infection safety?
questions.context: SHIFT NOTE — Visitor is coughing. Tissues and a waste bin are available. The nearby hand-cleaning dispenser is empty. The visitor’s coat is blue.
answers: A waste bin has a lid
questions.explanation: The empty dispenser directly affects access to hand hygiene; the coat colour is distracting information.

questions.question: Which is the clearest concise handover?
questions.context: NEW DETAIL — The person reports dizziness on standing. Observations were rechecked and qualified review was requested.
answers: They seem a bit odd today
New dizziness on standing; observations rechecked; qualified review requested
A long story with no time or action details
questions.explanation: The correct handover states the new symptom, what was checked and what action was requested without assumptions.

questions.question: An airway blockage prevents air reaching the lungs. What downstream effect follows most directly?
questions.context: Use the process: airway → lungs → blood → working tissues.

visual.ariaLabel: Airway blocked, less air to lungs, unknown, less oxygen to tissues

answers: The kidneys immediately form more urine
questions.explanation: If less air reaches the lungs, less oxygen can enter the blood and reach working tissues.

questions.question: A person drinks 0.75 L, then 425 mL. What total should be recorded in mL?
questions.context: Convert the first amount to millilitres, then combine both entries.

visual.ariaLabel: 0.75 litres plus 425 millilitres, total in millilitres

questions.question: What is the safest conclusion from this trend?
questions.context: Earlier: alert, normal colour, breathing comfortably. Now: confused, pale and breathing noticeably faster.
answers: There is clear deterioration requiring prompt qualified assessment
The trend is reassuring because no exact diagnosis is given
Wait for another shift before reporting it
questions.explanation: New confusion, pallor and faster breathing together show major deterioration from the earlier condition.

questions.question: Which response best addresses both stated risks?
questions.context: A task may splash body fluid towards the eyes. Shared equipment will then be used by another person.
answers: Wear ordinary clothing and skip equipment cleaning
Use appropriate eye or face protection, then clean shared equipment appropriately
Only wear gloves and leave the equipment for the next person
Avoid hand hygiene because eye protection was used
questions.explanation: The splash risk calls for suitable eye or face protection, while shared equipment needs appropriate cleaning before reuse.

questions.question: Which response meets both communication needs?
questions.context: A person says, “I’m frightened, and I didn’t understand what was explained.”
answers: Tell them the information was already given
Promise that nothing bad can happen
Acknowledge the fear, explain plainly and check their understanding
Ask someone else to answer without the person present
questions.explanation: The best response addresses the emotion, uses plain language and confirms understanding.

questions.question: Who is the immediate priority?
questions.context: Person A has mild stable discomfort, is alert and is speaking normally. Person B has become difficult to wake, looks pale and is breathing irregularly.
answers: Person A, because discomfort always comes first
Both can wait for a routine check
Choose based on who arrived first
Person B, because consciousness and breathing have suddenly changed
questions.explanation: A sudden change in consciousness with irregular breathing signals immediate danger and needs urgent qualified help.
